home.title: One workspace. Multiple minds. Total control.
home.subtitle: DualCode is a next-generation IDE where AI agents collaborate, share context, and help developers build faster—without sacrificing transparency, privacy, or control.

why.title: Not another editor with a chat box.
why.body: A single assistant bolted onto an editor has one view of your project and one way of failing. DualCode starts from a different question: what if several agents could specialize, share useful context and hand work to each other — and every step stayed visible to you?
points: Specialized agents instead of one generalist.
Shared context that you can inspect and edit.
Permissions and confirmations before agents touch your files.
why.belief: We believe you should be able to see what every agent reads, decides and changes — and say no.

agents.title: Claude and Codex, in the same room.
agents.body: Agents work side by side in one workspace. One drafts, another reviews; one explores the codebase, another runs the checks. You read the transcript, approve what matters and redirect when you disagree.
agents.emblemAlt: DualCode logo: two heads facing each other inside an infinity loop, one orange with a spark and one teal with code brackets
agents.note: Provider availability depends on the accounts and tools you connect. Nothing here implies an official partnership with any provider.

privacy.title: Your workspace is yours.
privacy.body: DualCode is designed so the product itself does not phone home by default, and so project memory lives on your machine first. These are design principles we are building towards; the Transparency page tracks what is actually implemented.
privacy.caveat: Be precise about this: when you use a cloud model, the prompts and context you send go to that provider. DualCode having no telemetry does not change what a provider receives.

quantum.title: Context retrieval, organised locally.
quantum.body: DualQuantum is a technology in development focused on retrieving the right context, organising knowledge on your machine and spending fewer resources doing it. We will publish numbers only when we can reproduce them.

items.title: Multi-agent collaboration
items.body: Several agents work in one workspace, split the job by strength and hand work to each other instead of competing for your cursor.

items.title: Transparency
items.body: Every step is a readable transcript: what an agent read, what it changed and why. Nothing happens off-screen.

items.title: Privacy first
items.body: No analytics and no third-party scripts on this site, and no product telemetry by design. Cloud models still receive what you send them.

items.title: Local memory
items.body: Project notes and context are meant to live on your machine first, where you can inspect, edit and delete them.

items.title: Security and permissions
items.body: Agents ask before they write files or run commands. Permission scopes are being designed and are not final.

items.title: Enterprise vision

privacy.title: Your workspace is yours.
privacy.subtitle: These are the privacy principles DualCode is built around. They are design goals. The Transparency page tracks what is actually implemented, and until something is verified we do not present it as a guarantee.

sections.title: No telemetry by default
sections.body: The goal is that DualCode itself sends no usage telemetry unless you choose to turn something on.

sections.title: Local-first memory
sections.body: Project memory and notes are meant to live on your machine first, in a form you can inspect.

sections.title: Control over stored context
sections.body: You should be able to see and change what is remembered.
items: Decide what is shared between agents.

sections.title: Permissions and confirmations
sections.body: Agents should ask before they change files or run commands, and you should be able to review what they did afterwards.

sections.title: Provider transparency
sections.body: When you connect a cloud model provider, the prompts and project context needed for a request are sent to that provider and handled under its own terms. This is separate from DualCode's own telemetry, and we cannot make promises about a provider's practices. Read their policies.

sections.title: Clear retention and deletion
sections.body: You should be able to tell how long something is kept and delete it. The exact mechanics will be documented once they exist.

siteItems: No analytics, advertising pixels or tracking scripts. Fonts and images are served from the site itself.
Your language choice is saved in your browser's local storage under the key dualcode.lang. It stays on your device.

The site is prepared for Cloudflare Pages hosting. Cloudflare, like any host, may keep standard technical request logs to run its infrastructure. That is separate from the site code and from the DualCode application.
This is not a formal privacy policy. A legal policy still needs human review before it is published.
privacy.limits: What we are not saying: that nothing ever leaves your computer, that DualCode works fully offline, or that any provider handles your data in a particular way.

sections.title: Where your data goes
sections.body: Two different things are easy to mix up.
items: Stored locally: the intent is that project memory and settings stay on your machine. What is stored today will be listed here once confirmed.
Sent to providers: if you use a cloud model, the prompts and context for each request go to that provider. DualCode having no telemetry does not change that.

sections.title: Telemetry, in plain language
sections.body: Our goal is that DualCode does not report your usage back to us unless you opt in. This is a principle until we can verify and document it. This website uses no analytics.

sections.title: Licensing and dependencies
sections.body: No source licence is declared on this site, so we do not describe DualCode as open source. Dependency and licence information will be published here when the project makes it available.

sections.title: Testing and reporting problems
sections.body: This website is checked with automated browser tests and manual visual review before it is published. A dedicated security contact has not been published yet. Until then, do not send sensitive vulnerability details through public channels.

sections.title: Assigning and checking work
sections.body: The orchestrator is meant to break a request into tasks, give each to the agent best suited to it, and collect the results. Results are not trusted by default: another agent or you review them before they land.

sections.title: Three things that are easy to confuse
sections.body: Keeping these apart is central to the design.
items: Persistent memory: knowledge about your project that lasts between sessions and is meant to stay on your machine.
Session context: what the agents are looking at right now, which disappears when the session ends.
Model provider: the service that runs a model. It only sees what is sent in a request.

sections.title: DualQuantum
sections.body: A technology in development focused on retrieving the right context, organising knowledge locally and being efficient while doing it. We do not publish token or speed figures until we can reproduce them.

sections.title: What we do not claim
sections.body: No benchmarks, savings percentages or comparisons with other tools are stated on this site, because none have been measured and published yet.

notes: A Windows x64 installer with the DualCode IDE and its agent panel.
A welcome screen and an agent side panel. With no project open, the panel asks you to open a folder so it can write .dualcode/transcript.md and run Codex or Claude from the project root.
Once a folder is open, the panel offers a Team mode with Codex and Claude.
The helper tools are included: Node v24.18.0, gemini-cli 0.66.0, opencode 1.19.4 (a baseline build that does not require AVX2) and MinGit.
The installer is trimmed to reduce its size: source maps, extra locales and some extensions are left out.
limits: Beta quality: it has not been through a stable release process.
Windows x64 only. There is no macOS or Linux build.

faq.title: Straight answers.
faq.subtitle: Short, honest answers about what DualCode is and is not today. If a feature is not built yet, we say so.

items.a: DualCode is an IDE built around AI agents that collaborate in one workspace while the developer stays in control. It is in beta: a Windows pre-release is available and there is no stable release yet.
Yes, as a beta. The Download page offers the Windows x64 installer for 1.143.1-beta.4 with its SHA-256. It is a pre-release and is not code-signed.
No pricing has been announced. We will not publish plans or prices until they are real and final.

items.q: Which AI models does it use?
items.a: DualCode is designed to coordinate several agents, such as Claude and Codex. Which providers work depends on the accounts and tools you connect. Nothing here implies an official partnership with any provider.

items.q: Does my code leave my machine?
items.a: The design goal is local-first: project memory is kept on your machine and the product itself does not phone home by default. When you use a cloud model, the prompts and context you send go to that provider. The Transparency page tracks what is actually implemented.
No. It loads no analytics, ad pixels or third-party scripts. The only thing it stores in your browser is your language choice, so the site opens in the language you picked.

items.q: Is the Interactive Preview the real product?
items.a: No. It is a front-end-only concept. It calls no model and every output in it is scripted, to show how agents, tasks and local memory could fit together.
Not today. Team and enterprise capabilities are a planned or long-term direction and carry no dates, prices or certifications.
A team of five people. The Team page shows their handles as supplied; roles and biographies appear only once each person confirms them.
The Roadmap lists each stage with its real status and no promised dates. Announcements go to the official Discord community.

dash.title: Watch a session unfold.
dash.body: A scripted session of two agents and one developer: routing, reading, editing, testing, review, an approval gate and memory. It is a simulation of the idea, not a recording of a released build.
dash.label: Simulated DualCode workspace session
dash.srSummary: Simulated session. A developer asks for session expiry on the auth module. The orchestrator routes planning to Claude and implementation to Codex. They read the code, plan, edit two files, run tests, review the diff and fix a clock-skew edge case, then ask the developer for permission before applying changes.
